alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a white-haired, clean-shaven man in a dark double-breasted coat, white collar and tie, looking at the camera. The card below is printed "The Late Lord Bishop of Massachusetts, The Right Rev. Phillips Brooks, D.D." and "Elliott & Fry", with a library stamp at the lower right of the photograph.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de un hombre de pelo blanco y sin barba, con levita oscura cruzada, cuello blanco y corbata, que mira a la cámara. En la tarjeta, debajo, está impreso "The Late Lord Bishop of Massachusetts, The Right Rev. Phillips Brooks, D.D." y "Elliott & Fry", con un sello de biblioteca abajo a la derecha de la foto.

caption.en: Phillips Brooks, who wrote the words, photographed by Elliott & Fry of London in about 1887 to 1892; the card names him "The Late Lord Bishop of Massachusetts", the office he held from 1891 until his death in 1893.
caption.es: Phillips Brooks, autor de la letra, fotografiado por Elliott & Fry, de Londres, hacia 1887 a 1892; la tarjeta lo llama "The Late Lord Bishop of Massachusetts" (el difunto obispo de Massachusetts), cargo que ocupó desde 1891 hasta su muerte en 1893.

source: The late Lord Bishop of Massachusetts, the right Rev. Phillips Brooks, D. D. (cabinet photograph, print on card mount, 17 x 11 cm; "Elliott & Fry, photographers, 55, Baker Street, London. W.")
library: Boston Public Library, Cabinet Card Collection (via Digital Commonwealth)
licenceEvidence: Holder's record (https://www.digitalcommonwealth.org/search/commonwealth:8c97pm356): "No known copyright restrictions." and "No known restrictions on use." Photograph about 1887 to 1892 by the London firm Elliott & Fry (Joseph John Elliott died 1903, Clarence Edmund Fry died 1897; no individual operator named): PD by age (see rights.md).
credit: Boston Public Library, Cabinet Card Collection

alt.en: A black-and-white photograph looking across the flat stone roofs of houses, with trees in the foreground, to Bethlehem on its ridge: terraced gardens with stone walls on the left, large stone buildings and a square bell tower along the skyline, a slender minaret in the middle and a cone-shaped hill on the horizon.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro que mira por encima de los tejados planos de piedra de unas casas, con árboles en primer plano, hacia Belén sobre su loma: huertos en terrazas con muros de piedra a la izquierda, grandes edificios de piedra y un campanario cuadrado en el horizonte, un minarete esbelto en el centro y un cerro en forma de cono al fondo.

caption.en: Bethlehem, photographed by the American Colony of Jerusalem between about 1900 and 1920. When Brooks rode in on Christmas Eve 1865, he wrote home of a good-looking town on a ridge among terraced gardens.
caption.es: Belén, fotografiada por la American Colony de Jerusalén entre 1900 y 1920 aproximadamente. Cuando Brooks llegó a caballo la Nochebuena de 1865, escribió a casa que era un pueblo de buen aspecto sobre una loma, entre huertos en terrazas.

source: Bethlehem and surroundings. General view of Bethlehem. (glass negative, stereograph; one half shown, cropped)
library: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, G. Eric and Edith Matson Photograph Collection
licenceEvidence: LoC catalogue record LCCN 2019692465 (MARCXML read by the checker through LoC's SRU server lx2.loc.gov:210/lcdb), field 540: "No known restrictions on publication. (see rights.md).

alt.en: Part of a printed hymn-book page: hymn number 63, headed "II. 7. 8s & 6s." with a small line "Music in Parish Hymnal, p. 158, or p. 120; Sabbath Songs, p. 90.", then the words "O little town of Bethlehem" with a large initial O, in three numbered stanzas of eight lines, and no music.
alt.es: Parte de una página impresa de un himnario: el himno número 63, con el encabezado "II. 7. 8s & 6s." y una línea pequeña "Music in Parish Hymnal, p. 158, or p. 120; Sabbath Songs, p. 90.", y después la letra "O little town of Bethlehem", con una O inicial grande, en tres estrofas numeradas de ocho versos, sin música.

caption.en: The carol as No. 63 in the Sunday School Service and Hymn Book of the Episcopal Diocese of Ohio (New York, 1870), its earliest known printing in a book: no author's name and no music, only a line sending singers to two other books for a tune.
caption.es: El villancico como n.º 63 del Sunday School Service and Hymn Book de la diócesis episcopal de Ohio (Nueva York, 1870), su primera impresión conocida en un libro: sin nombre de autor y sin música, solo una línea que remite a los cantantes a otros dos libros para la melodía.

source: Sunday School Service and Hymn Book, Sunday School Committee of the Diocese of Ohio (New York: E. P. Dutton, 1870), p. 82, No. 63 (cropped to the hymn; stanzas 1 to 3, the rest on p. 83)
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1870 (IA record: "New York : E.P. Dutton and Co.", date 1870); words by Phillips Brooks, died 1893; corporate compiler (the diocese's Sunday School Committee). Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed hymn-book page headed "Christmas." in black-letter type, then "No. 43. ST. LOUIS. L. H. Redner.": four systems of music on treble and bass staves with the first verse, "O lit-tle town of Beth-le-hem!", under the notes, ending "A-men.", and verses 2, 3 and 4 printed below.
alt.es: Página impresa de un himnario con el encabezado "Christmas." en letra gótica y después "No. 43. ST. LOUIS. L. H. Redner.": cuatro sistemas de música en clave de sol y de fa con la primera estrofa, "O lit-tle town of Beth-le-hem!", bajo las notas, que terminan en "A-men.", y las estrofas 2, 3 y 4 impresas debajo.

caption.en: No. 43 in William Reed Huntington's The Church Porch (New York, 1874), the earliest known printing of words and tune together; Redner said it was Huntington who named the tune ST. LOUIS. It prints four stanzas, as American books have usually sung it since.
caption.es: El n.º 43 de The Church Porch de William Reed Huntington (Nueva York, 1874), la primera impresión conocida de letra y melodía juntas; Redner dijo que fue Huntington quien llamó ST. LOUIS a la melodía. Trae cuatro estrofas, como suelen cantarlo desde entonces los libros estadounidenses.

source: William Reed Huntington, The Church Porch: A Service Book and Hymnal for Sunday Schools (New York: E. P. Dutton, 1874), No. 43, "ST. LOUIS. L. H. Redner."
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1874 (IA record: "New York : E.P. Dutton", date 1874); editor William Reed Huntington died 1909, composer Lewis H. Redner died 1908, words by Phillips Brooks, died 1893. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive
